To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
kainate receptors are expressed by hippocampal neurons and that their properties are distinct from those of AMPA or NMDA receptors.
kainate receptors are not blocked by the non-NMDA receptor antagonist GYKI 53466, are not blocked by low concentrations of lanthanum, and are desensitized by SYM 208.

kainate receptor activation is characterized by rapid desensitization, slow recovery from desensitizaiton, and potentiation by Concanavalin-A, whereas AMPA receptors are not desensitized by SYM 208 1 or ConcanavalinA and do not show slow recovery from desentization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the synaptic transmission in the central nervous system.
the properties of the glutamate receptor that mediates fast excitatory synaptic transmission in the CNS.
the activation and desensitization properties of kainic acid (KA)-preferring receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the properties of these receptors, which are expressed by hippocampal neurons at early stages of their development, are distinct from the properties of homomeric GluR6 receptors expressed in oocytes.
kainate receptors, like AMPA receptors, are desensitizing glutamate-gated cation channels, but their properties are not identical to those of AMPA receptors.
the kainate receptors in the hippocampus have a complex structure, and the pharmacological profile is dependent on the developmental stage of the animal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kainate receptors of hippocampal neurons are composed of multiple subunits that display properties intermediate between those of GluR5 and GluR6.
the GluR5 subunit is expressed by hippocampal neurons at the age we examined and that it forms functional heteromeric assemblies with the GluR1 subunit.
the properties of native kainate receptors are intermediate between the GluR5 and GluR6 receptor subtypes, but that they are more similar to the GluR 5 subunit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
kainate receptors in hippocampal neurons are desensitized by SYM 2080, a compound that has been used as a selective antagonist for these receptors.
the kainate receptor expressed by neurons from the adult hippocampus is not a homomeric assembly of GluR6.
the kainate receptors in our hippocampal cultures are heteromultimeric assemblies of the Gluk1, Gluk2, and Gluk5 subunits.
